front.title: Framework and YANG Data Model for the NMA Northbound Task Interface (NTI)

author.organization: China Academy of Information and Communication Technology
China Academy of Information and Communications Technology

abstract.t:
This document describes a framework and a YANG data model for the Northbound Task Interface (NTI) of a Network Management Agent (NMA). The NTI is a logical northbound interface through which upper-layer consumers, including OSS/BSS, orchestrators, management applications, and other agents, can submit network management tasks to an NMA and obtain task processing results.
This document specifies a YANG-based realization of the NTI, including operational state data, RPC operations, and notifications for capability discovery, intent submission, task lifecycle management, execution plan exposure, confirmation handling, and result reporting. The model is intended to reuse existing IETF network management models for domain-specific information.
The NTI does not mandate a dedicated communication protocol. NETCONF and RESTCONF can be used for the YANG-based realization, while A2A- based mechanisms may also be used to realize NTI interactions. This document does not define or extend generic agent interaction protocols.
